instruction: networkx's ISMAGS class (networkx/algorithms/isomorphism/ismags.py) finds isomorphisms, subgraph isomorphisms and largest common subgraphs, but not monomorphisms. Add ISMAGS.monomorphisms_iter(symmetry=True), a generator of mappings, and ISMAGS.is_monomorphic(symmetry=False), True when at least one exists. For ISMAGS(graph, subgraph, node_match, edge_match), a monomorphism maps every subgraph node to a distinct graph node so that each subgraph edge lands on a graph edge (in the same direction for directed graphs) and node and edge attributes match; unlike a subgraph isomorphism, graph edges between mapped nodes that have no subgraph counterpart are allowed. Mappings are dicts from graph nodes to subgraph nodes, the orientation subgraph_isomorphisms_iter uses. In multigraphs, k parallel edges between two subgraph nodes (or k self-loops on one) need at least k between their images, in the same direction. With symmetry=False the mappings are exactly those that GraphMatcher(graph, subgraph, node_match=..., edge_match=...).subgraph_monomorphisms_iter() yields (DiGraphMatcher for directed graphs), for Graph, DiGraph, MultiGraph and MultiDiGraph; with symmetry=True, mappings that differ only by a symmetry of the subgraph are yielded once, as subgraph_isomorphisms_iter(symmetry=True) does. Existing ISMAGS results (is_isomorphic, isomorphisms_iter, subgraph_is_isomorphic, subgraph_isomorphisms_iter, largest_common_subgraph) must not change. Add tests.
